riskTone.label: BULLISH
riskTone.rationale: Cool US inflation, solid bank earnings, and easing tariff threats via Russia sanctions bill all support risk-on sentiment for UK100.

briefing.briefing: Starting with sterling (GBP): GBPUSD is almost flat today, up just +0.03%, which the snapshot flags as NEUTRAL for UK100 — meaning the currency isn't meaningfully helping or hurting the index right now via the usual sign-flip (where a weaker pound boosts big multinationals that earn in dollars). The key forces shaping today's session are a broadly supportive backdrop: banks are the standout bullish sector, because the 10-year gilt yield [the UK government's borrowing rate over 10 years, a benchmark for bank profitability] has risen 8 basis points [hundredths of a percent], which helps banks earn more on their lending — HSBC, Barclays, NatWest and StanChart are all big index weights. Long-end gilt stress is NOT flagged, so this yield rise looks like a healthy rotation rather than a fiscal alarm bell. Energy (Brent oil -0.24%) and miners (copper +0.37%) are both reading NEUTRAL, meaning they're neither a tailwind nor a drag. Pharma remains idiosyncratic — AstraZeneca can swing the index on its own, and no specific AZN catalyst is visible in the data today. On the US side, the S&P 500 is up +0.25% today and the VIX [a 'fear gauge' for US markets] sits at 17.32 in NORMAL regime — no stress signal. The recent catalysts (from the last 24 hours) include cool US inflation data and solid US bank earnings lifting Wall Street overnight (23.9 hours ago), and a Reuters report that a Russia sanctions bill is easing tariff threats on China and India (11.4 hours ago) — both are genuinely risk-positive reads for UK100 via improved global growth sentiment and commodity demand. GBP positioning data (futures traders are crowded short sterling [meaning many are betting the pound falls], a contrarian BEARISH signal for FTSE because a short squeeze in GBP could hurt the index) is the main bearish offset. Directional bias leans mildly BULLISH — the macro backdrop is supportive, US equities are constructive, and gilts are helping banks — but conviction is only MEDIUM because sterling is near 89th percentile of its 20-day range [close to its recent highs], crowded short positioning could unwind sharply, and UK GDP data drops at 07:00 BST tomorrow which could reprice everything. Confidence: 5/10 — the GDP print tomorrow is the single biggest variable; a weak number could flip the script quickly, while a beat would add fuel. On the ORB specifically: the 08:00 opening range broke DOWN (ORB low at 10,449, ORB high at 10,471.3), yet UK100 has since recovered to 10,501 — above the overnight high of 10,490.6 — meaning the initial bearish break has FAILED and price has reversed above structure; this is a classic fakeout/sweep-then-reverse pattern, and the bullish macro backdrop supports treating the failed breakdown as a long signal rather than chasing any fresh short. Event risk today appears light (no scheduled UK/US events flagged for today), but TOMORROW's UK GDP Monthly Estimate at 07:00 BST is HIGH-impact and arrives just one hour before the cash open — traders should size down or stand aside on any pre-GDP positions. Key levels to watch: ORB high 10,471.3 (now support after the failed breakdown), overnight high 10,490.6 (also flipped to support), current price 10,501.25, prior day high 10,545.1 (next meaningful resistance), and ORB low 10,449 / overnight low 10,431.2 as the invalidation zone if bulls lose control; with 14-day average daily range [how far the index typically moves in a day] at 130.9 points and 59% already used, roughly 54 points of range remain — enough for a meaningful move but not a full trend day. The one thing to remember today: the ORB broke down and then snapped back above 10,490 — in a bullish macro environment, failed breakdowns are often the trade, but tomorrow's GDP at 07:00 means tonight is not the night to hold large positions overnight.
